draft: NEW DRAFT 3.0-draft1 by Board Master, rebuilt from standard shop practice after the 2026-10-13 data loss. NOT 2.5.3.2. Values marked shopDefault:true are my defaults, not recovered values.
description: Random offcuts milled to one thickness and glued end grain up.

steps.title: Mill rough stock
steps.description: Joint one face and one edge on the jointer, then plane to final thickness plus 1/8" (3 mm). Rest overnight, then plane to final thickness. Take ~1/64" (0.4 mm) passes for the last two passes.
safetyBanners: WARNING: Use push blocks on the jointer. Never joint stock shorter than 12" (305 mm) or thinner than 1/2" (12.5 mm).
WARNING: Keep hands clear of the infeed and outfeed. Feed only boards at least 12" (305 mm) long.

steps.title: Sort offcuts
steps.description: Discard pieces with checks, knots or softwood. Mill everything to the same thickness.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use closed-grain, non-toxic hardwoods only. Avoid spalted, softwood or oily/sensitising exotics on cutting surfaces.

steps.title: Glue up
steps.description: Glue offcuts into rough panels. Alternate clamps above and below the panel and check for flat with a straightedge.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use a waterproof PVA glue rated for indirect food contact. Clamp until squeeze-out turns rubbery, then scrape.

steps.title: Crosscut slices
steps.description: Crosscut slices on a crosscut sled with a stop block.
safetyBanners: DANGER: Never use the rip fence as a length stop for crosscuts. Use a crosscut sled with a stop block set before the blade, so the offcut is never trapped between blade and fence.
WARNING: Do not cut pieces shorter than 6" (152 mm) free-hand on the table saw. Use a sled with a hold-down.

steps.title: Glue up
steps.description: Glue slices end grain up in random order. Alternate clamps above and below the panel and check for flat with a straightedge.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use a waterproof PVA glue rated for indirect food contact. Clamp until squeeze-out turns rubbery, then scrape.

steps.title: Flatten and sand
steps.description: Flatten with a router sled or drum sander, never the thickness planer. Sand 80, 120, 180 grit. Break edges (180 grit).
safetyBanners: DANGER: Never run an end-grain glue-up through the thickness planer. It can blow apart. Flatten with a router sled or drum sander.

steps.title: Edge profile
steps.description: Rout the edge profile, default: 1/8" (3 mm) roundover. Optional finger grips: core box / round-nose bit 3/8–1/2" (10–12 mm).
safetyBanners: WARNING: Climb cuts can grab. Feed the router against the bit rotation and take shallow passes.

steps.title: Finish
steps.description: Raise the grain with a damp cloth, sand 180 again, then flood with food-safe mineral oil and top with board butter.
safetyBanners: NOTE: Use closed-grain, non-toxic hardwoods only. Avoid spalted, softwood or oily/sensitising exotics on cutting surfaces.

notes: Take ~1/64" (0.4 mm) passes for final surfacing.
